dog.description_text:
This is Lucy! She is the most loving, fun, and adaptable little lady that we have ever fostered. From the moment she arrived, she snuggled up to us, played with our resident dogs, and explored her new home and neighborhood with unwavering confidence.

Personality and Characteristics:

Lucy is undeniably adorable. Her exuberant wagging tail and gentle kisses melt our hearts. On her first night home, she nuzzled her way under my blanket and curled up on my lap for cuddles. Lucy is an affable and confident pup who effortlessly follows our daily routines, whether they’re familiar or new. She greets dogs and people with calm optimism and without discrimination. She even loves me and my husband equally! Lucy is a playful pup who enjoys going on walks, but she’s also content to stay home alone for hours without any issue. We’ve been amazed to see how Lucy embraces every moment like a dream dog!

Sociability with people and dogs: Great!

Lucy has met a wide range of people, dogs, and noises and she’s done exceptionally well with them all. Whenever someone greets her, she responds with a cautious sniff then a wagging tail. Her interactions with dogs are also quite balanced and positive given her tiny size. When she sees a dog during our walk, she either politely walks past them when necessary, but when they stop to say hello, she greets them with a calm sniff regardless of their size or energy level. She does let new dogs know that she is not to be trifled with by making herself as adorably tall as possible. Occasionally she gets nervous and barks at a certain person or dog in the distance, but once I remind her to be calm, she regulates herself and continues on. She is learning quickly to be calm and confident on walks and we are very impressed with her progress.

When we first brought Lucy home, she introduced herself to our resident dogs as the new pack leader. After some playful greetings, they tried a couple different status configurations, and the group quickly settled into a new hierarchy without any issues. Now, they all cuddle together, feeling secure and affectionate towards their tiny pack member. We haven’t seen Lucy have a big play session with our dogs, but she definitely likes their company.

Lucy is highly trainable when we correct her during interactions. For instance, when she made a few ill-placed territorial growls at our resident dog or visiting friend, she promptly submitted and moved on. Lucy is a bit wary when a new person approaches us or our dogs at home. However, she was easily reassured that she didn’t need to guard us when. I think it would be good for her future adopter to be proactive in preventing resource guarding since it can be a trait in little dogs.

Potty Training:

Lucy is a star student in potty training. For the first two days, she had zero accidents inside, which is a remarkable sign for becoming an a very well potty trained dog once fully settled. She has had a few minor accidents, but overall she shows a lot of potential. She enthusiastically goes potty outside without any hesitation or nerves, even in the bustling city. She also uses pee pads when needed. When it comes to holding pee over night, we have been very impressed with her ability to comfortably sleep in for up to 9 hours before requesting a walk!

Crate training:

Lucy enjoys our crate, but we have not yet locked her in it. Currently, she sleeps in our bed and absolutely loves being curled up under the blanket with us.

Keywords for Lucy:

CUTE, secure, loving, smart, fun, and very adaptable to change.

Energy levels: 5 (1= calm, 10= Lucy is a high-energy dog.)

She is a 1 when we’re relaxing on the sofa and a 9 when it’s time to play or go for a walk.

Barker? Or Quiet Pup?: Normal

She’ll give some warning-bark/growls at things she thinks are questionable, but it feels more like communication than aggression or defensiveness. She has been excellent about no barking when home alone. She does use a grumble and occasional bark when she is frustrated or anxious about something.

Walking Manners:

Lucy is an enthusiastic walker and gets very excited to go on a walk when we get the leash. She’s pretty brave in the city and walks at a spunky little trot. We have been exposing her to lots of different noises and reinforcing her relaxation around them with treats. It is going really well and she even is learning “heel!” Lucy has excellent stamina and grit in walks. She continues to explore and trot alone regardless of weather or noises. If you want to take your dog on extra long walks from time to time, she would be a great candidate. She is also perfectly content to take short walks and she turns around to come home whenever needed.

Appetite: Excellent.

She arrived underweight but she eats great.

Commands/Tricks:

Lucy is excellent at recall. She is the first dog we’ve had who always comes when called. It’s great! She is also pretty good with leave it, back, stay and other directional commands. We are training her to sit, and she is learning it quickly. She is a genius on walks at stepping over the leash to keep it from tangling with her legs.

Favorite Things:

She adores people and hanging out. While she loves to get attention, and will happily play or curl up with you whenever possible, she is also great at being independent. She likes beef cheek rolls and seems interested in squeaky toys. She really is the sweetest little snuggle bug and she will be a great love to whoever is lucky enough to bring her in to their home.

To adopt Lucy
ALL adoptions require a completed application and final contract. The application can be found at WaldosRescue.org and once you are approved to adopt you will be put in touch with the foster to see if it’s a good match. We are a RESCUE not a shelter. We conduct veterinary and personal reference checks during the application approval process. We are unable to contact every applicant for every dog. We will select the best applicant for each dog, based on the dogs needs. Waldos Rescue Pen is a 501c3 whose primary focus is rescuing dogs from the euthanasia list from high kill shelters throughout the United States and Korea.
